title: Spiral Prioritization: Token-Velocity Elasticity Framework for Roadmap Allocation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a Spiral Prioritization framework that ranks initiatives by combining RICE-style impact with a token-velocity elasticity term and a latency/cost fragility modifier. The goal is to produce a reproducible rubric for roadmap allocation that directly ties feature investment to inference unit economics and operational risk, enabling trade-offs between product value and serving costs to be surfaced quantitatively.
motivation: Current RICE variants at Redwood surface impact and reach but frequently miss the operational economics signal (token velocity, batching gains, latency SLO pressure). This leads to under/over-investing in features with hidden per-token costs. The Spiral framework folds an elasticity term that models how incremental traffic changes affect per-token unit cost and latency to better prioritize work that optimizes product value per marginal dollar spent.
scoring_components: Reach (R) — estimated weekly active requests affected, normalized to cohort (0-10).
Impact (I) — qualitative-to-quantitative estimate of end-user benefit on a 0-10 scale with justification.
Confidence (C) — evidence score 0-10 (A/B tests, pilot telemetry, customer interviews).
Effort (E) — estimated story points, converted to an inverse 0-10 value using a curve (lower effort -> higher score).
Token-Velocity Elasticity (TVE) — multiplier (0.5–2.0) estimating percent change in per-token cost when traffic changes; derived from historical batching/throughput analysis for similar endpoints.
Latency Fragility (LF) — penalty (0–3) applied when initiative risks increasing p95 latency beyond SLO thresholds; higher for chat-heavy, low-latency flows.
Final spiral score formula: ((R * I * C) / E) * TVE - LF.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible calculator (spreadsheet + notebook) that computes the spiral score given input fields and historical throughput metrics.
A one-page playbook for product and engineering describing how to estimate TVE and LF for typical feature types (generation APIs, embeddings, bulk batch jobs).
A validation run applying the framework to the next quarter's top 25 candidate initiatives with documented score-driven recommendations.
Stakeholder review and sign-off from Eng Reliability, Finance, and Developer Experience teams.
risks: TVE estimations may be noisy for greenfield features with no analogue — mitigated by assigning conservative confidence and running small pilot traffic tests.
Over-penalizing latency-fragile features could bias against low-latency product improvements; include explicit hooks for strategic exceptions with exec review.
Framework complexity may slow decision cadence — deliver a streamlined 'fast-pass' variant for <3 day decisions that uses coarse buckets.
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with PM, Eng Reliability, Finance; agreed on core components and data sources (billing, console latency dashboards, batching telemetry).

2026-02-27: Prototype TVE estimator built by Data Science (notebook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/TVE-Estimator) — initial elasticity ranges (0.8-1.6) for generation endpoints based on 6 months of telemetry.
2026-03-03: Design review — clarified LF penalty application for streaming chat vs non-streaming generation; Design requested examples for in-console guidance.
2026-03-07: Finance reviewed formula and asked for mapping from spiral score to budget allocation buckets (High/Medium/Low). Assigned follow-up to Finance (task ENG-19871 for budget mapping).

2026-03-10: Internal dry run: applied Spiral scoring to 12 candidate initiatives; produced a recommended Q2 allocation draft and flagged three initiatives for small-scale pilot testing to validate TVE. Links: GH PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap/pull/342, Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Spiral-Prioritization-Draft.
decisions: Adopt TVE as a multiplicative factor rather than additive to reflect compounding cost effects at scale.
Use p95 latency as primary signal for LF penalty; secondary monitoring for error-rate impact.
Require minimum confidence score of 4 for any initiative to be auto-accepted by the fast-pass variant; lower confidence routes to pilot stage.
review_feedback: Eng Reliability: asked for automated extraction of batching and KV cache hit rates to improve TVE accuracy.
Finance: requested mapping from spiral score to a 3-tier budget allocation and a short rationale field for exceptions.
Developer Experience: suggested adding a README and quick-start template so PMs can estimate TVE using console exports.
